## Overview

This is an OfficeFloor-based Spring PetClinic variant. `POST /api/owners` is orchestrated declaratively as a pipeline of single-responsibility functions defined in a YAML file, with duplicate detection implemented as three separate "Reject*" functions (email, telephone, household) that each throw a checked exception mapped to HTTP 409 by a matching handler. DTOs (`OwnerFieldsDto`, `OwnerDto`) are generated at build time from `openapi.yml`.

## 1 & 4. The POST /api/owners pipeline (OfficeFloor YAML)

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml` — defines the full create flow. Duplicate-detection steps run in this order (lines 20-30), each `next`-chained:
- `rejectDuplicateEmail` -> `rejectDuplicateTelephone` -> `rejectDuplicateHousehold` -> `rejectCityAtCapacity` -> `rejectDailyLimit` -> `build` -> `assignNamesakeCount` -> `assignCustomerCode` -> `assignHousehold` -> `assignHouseholdSize` -> `save` -> `audit` -> `respond`.
- Endpoint is authorized via `authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"` (line 2).
- Normalization steps run first: `RequireOwnerFields` -> `NormalizeOwnerTelephone` -> `ValidateTelephoneCountryLength` -> `NormalizeOwnerEmail`, so the duplicate checks compare already-normalized values.

Other owner YAML endpoints: `owners.GET.yml`, `owners/{ownerId}.GET|PUT|DELETE.yml`, `owners/{ownerId}/pets.POST.yml`, plus `api/v2/owners.GET.yml`.

## 1 & 2. Duplicate-detection function classes

All under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/`:

- `RejectDuplicateEmail.java` — skips if email null; lowercases (Locale.ROOT) and compares against every `ownerRepository.findAll()`; throws `DuplicateEmailException` on collision (lines 20-35).
- `RejectDuplicateTelephone.java` — compares request E.164 telephone against `E164Telephone.normalizeOrNull(existing.getTelephone())` for every owner; throws `DuplicateTelephoneException` (lines 17-26).
- `RejectDuplicateHousehold.java` — household = same normalized last name (trim, collapse whitespace, lowercase) AND same `AddressNormalizer.normalize(address)`. Bypassed when request sets `sharesHousehold=true`; else throws `DuplicateHouseholdException` (lines 19-40).

Supporting normalization/assignment:
- `NormalizeOwnerTelephone.java` — mutates body to E.164 in place; 400 via `InvalidTelephoneException`.
- `NormalizeOwnerEmail.java` — validates syntax (regex line 25), lowercases, blank->null; 400 via `InvalidEmailException`.
- `E164Telephone.java` — utility: `normalize` (assumes `+61` when no country code, drops leading 0, 8-15 digits), `validateNationalNumberLength` (+61=>9, +1=>10), `normalizeOrNull` (lines 23-80).
- `AddressNormalizer.java` — canonical address: trim/collapse/uppercase + expand ST->STREET, RD->ROAD, AVE->AVENUE (used by both household reject and household-id assignment).
- `AssignHousehold.java` — when `sharesHousehold=true` and a match exists, derives a deterministic `householdId = UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes(lastName + "\n" + address)` and backfills all members (lines 27-53).

Note: All three duplicate checks iterate `ownerRepository.findAll()` in-memory (O(n) per create). There is no `normalizedTelephone`/`identityKey` column or index — matching is done by normalizing each existing owner on the fly.

## 2 & 3. Owner entity/model

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java` (`@Entity`, table `owners`). Fields: `address`, `city`, `telephone` (line 45-49; `@Pattern ^\+[0-9]{8,15}$` E.164), `email` (51-52), `registrationDate` (54-55), `customerCode` (57-58), `householdId` (60-61, column `household_id`), `namesakeCount` (63-64), `householdSize` (66-67), `pets` (OneToMany). Inherits `firstName`/`lastName` from `Person.java` (`@Column first_name`/`last_name`).

There is NO `deleted`/soft-delete field on the model and `DeleteOwner.java` calls `ownerRepository.delete(owner)` (hard delete) — this contradicts the `AcceptanceBase` comment (line 194-195) claiming soft-delete records are retained and ignored by duplicate checks. Worth flagging if soft-delete-aware duplicate detection is expected.

## 2. Exceptions and 409 handlers

Under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/escalation/`:
- `DuplicateEmailException.java` / `DuplicateEmailHandler.java` — handler sends `HttpStatus.CONFLICT` (409).
- `DuplicateTelephoneException.java` / `DuplicateTelephoneHandler.java` — 409.
- `DuplicateHouseholdException.java` / `DuplicateHouseholdHandler.java` — 409.

Each handler: `response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.CONFLICT))`. Related 400 handlers also exist: `InvalidEmailHandler`, `InvalidTelephoneHandler`, `MissingOwnerFieldsHandler`, plus `DataIntegrityViolationExceptionHandler`, `CityAtCapacityHandler`, `DailyLimitExceededHandler`.

## 5. Tests for owner duplicate detection

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java` — the only functional test. `coreRejectsIdentityCollision()` (lines 11-17) creates an owner, then a second owner reusing the first's telephone, asserting `status().isConflict()` (409). The class-level comment (line 7) describes a target: "Consolidate all duplicate detection into a single derived 'identityKey' = normalizedTeleph..." — i.e. the current three-check design is intended to be unified into one `identityKey`. This is the only place `identityKey`/`normalizedTelephone` appear in the codebase (both only as comments, not implemented).

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java` — black-box harness: builds owner JSON via `ownerNode()` (unique across all rules), posts to `POST /api/owners`, reads back via `GET`. `@Transactional` rollback per test. ## 6. Response DTOs for owners

DTOs are generated (MapStruct + OpenAPI generator) from `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — no hand-written DTO source exists in `src`:
- `OwnerFields` schema (lines 1991-2057): input fields incl. `telephone` (pattern `^[0-9]*$`), `email`, `registrationDate`, and write-only `sharesHousehold` (2046-2051). Required: firstName, lastName, address, city, telephone.

The response is assembled in `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/RespondWithOwnerCreated.java` — maps Owner->`OwnerDto` via `OwnerMapper`, sets `bulkSignupWarning`, returns `201 Created` with `Location: /api/owners/{id}` (lines 15-20).

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — MapStruct mapper deriving `displayName`, `initials`, `membershipNumber`, `membershipLevel`, `locality`, `contactPreference`; `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` ignores id/pets/customerCode/householdId/namesakeCount/householdSize (lines 85-91).

## Key file paths summary
- Pipeline: `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/owners.POST.yml`
- Duplicate checks: `.../rest/function/owner/RejectDuplicate{Email,Telephone,Household}.java`
- Normalizers: `.../owner/NormalizeOwner{Telephone,Email}.java`, `E164Telephone.java`, `AddressNormalizer.java`
- Household id: `.../owner/AssignHousehold.java`
- Model: `.../model/Owner.java`, `.../model/Person.java`
- Exceptions/handlers: `.../rest/escalation/Duplicate{Email,Telephone,Household}{Exception,Handler}.java`
- Repository: `.../repository/OwnerRepository.java`
- DTO source of truth: `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` (lines 1991-2144)
- Mapper/response: `.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java`, `.../owner/RespondWithOwnerCreated.java`
- Tests: `src/test/java/.../acceptance/AcceptanceTest.java`, `AcceptanceBase.java`

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          pattern: '^[0-9]*$'
          example: '6085551023'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. Optional on create; when omitted the server's current date is used.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true, allows creating this owner even though another owner has the same last name and address (they share a household). Write-only; not stored.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: "Franklin, George"
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: "G.F."
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3 is the upper-cased first three letters of the city, LAST3 the upper-cased first three letters of the last name and NNNN a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence (one more than the owners already in that city).
              type: string
              example: "LON-SMI-0007"
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: A stable shared identifier for owners who share a household (same last name and address). Assigned when an owner opts in with sharesHousehold and an existing owner shares the household; every member carries the same value. Null for owners not in a shared household.
              type: string
              example: "5f2b3c1a-8d4e-3f6a-9b2c-1d0e7a5f4c33"
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: The number of existing owners (before this owner was created) sharing the same firstName and lastName, compared case-insensitively.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: "LON-SMI-0007-M26"
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: The owner's numeric membership level, from 1 to 3, computed on creation. Starts at 1; add 1 when an email is present; add 1 when namesakeCount is 0; capped at 3 (level 4 is reserved for tenure).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 3
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: The owner's locality (region), derived from the city via the fixed city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD). 'UNKNOWN' when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: "NSW"
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: True when more than 80 owners have already been created for today's business day (a bulk sign-up), otherwise false.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: The owner's preferred contact channel, 'EMAIL' when an email is present, otherwise 'PHONE'.
              type: string
              example: "EMAIL"
              readOnly: true
          required:
            - pets

## What I did

Consolidated the three separate duplicate checks (telephone, email, household) into a single `identityKey`-based check on `POST /api/owners`.

**Core concept** — `identityKey = normalizedTelephone + '|' + (email or empty) + '|' + (householdId or empty)`, computed identically for every owner. Two owners collide only when their **whole** keys are equal.

**New files**
- `OwnerIdentity.java` — shared utility deriving the key from an `Owner` (or raw parts); telephone normalized to E.164, email lower-cased, null email/household → empty segment.
- `RejectDuplicateIdentity.java` — the single consolidated check: computes the new owner's key and rejects a full-key match against existing owners with 409.
- `DuplicateIdentityException.java` + `DuplicateIdentityHandler.java` + its escalation YAML — the 409 response.

**Modified**
- `owners.POST.yml` — removed `rejectDuplicateEmail/Telephone/Household`; inserted `rejectDuplicateIdentity` **after** `assignHousehold` (governed by the transaction) so the new owner's `householdId` is already assigned when its key is computed, and before `save` so it can't collide with itself.
- `OwnerMapper.java` + `openapi.yml` — added the read-only `identityKey` field to the response, derived via `OwnerIdentity.key`.

**Removed** — the three old `RejectDuplicate*` functions, their exceptions/handlers, and their escalation YAMLs.

## Why this satisfies the spec
- The single key drives all duplicate detection; the three separate checks are gone.
- Because the telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same `householdId`) with **different** telephones produce different keys and are both allowed — only an exact full-key match is a 409.
- Placing the check after `assignHousehold` means the key uses each owner's real stored `householdId`, keeping the comparison symmetric between the new and existing owners.

The provided acceptance test (`coreRejectsIdentityCollision` — second owner reusing the first's telephone, no email, no household → identical keys → 409) passes.

Note: the `AcceptanceBase` helper comment references a soft-delete on `DELETE /api/owners/{id}`, but `DeleteOwner` currently hard-deletes and there's no `deleted` flag on the model — outside this change's scope, but worth flagging if soft-delete-aware identity checks are later expected.
